source: U.S. DOL Consolidated Minimum Wage Table (current as of July 2026).

AL.note: No state minimum wage law; federal floor applies.

CO.note: Denver and some localities set higher local rates.

GA.note: State law sets $5.15, but FLSA-covered employers must pay the $7.25 federal floor.

LA.note: No state minimum wage law; federal floor applies.

MN.note: Minneapolis and some localities set higher local rates.

MS.note: No state minimum wage law; federal floor applies.

MT.note: Lower rate applies to certain small businesses not covered by the FLSA.

NJ.note: Lower rate applies to seasonal and small employers.

NY.note: $17.00 in NYC, Long Island & Westchester; $16.00 in the rest of the state.

OH.note: Lower rate applies to smaller employers below a gross-receipts threshold.

OR.note: $16.80 in the Portland metro area, $15.55 standard, $14.55 in nonurban counties; adjusts annually July 1.

SC.note: No state minimum wage law; federal floor applies.

TN.note: No state minimum wage law; federal floor applies.

WA.note: Some cities (e.g., Seattle, Tukwila) set higher local rates.

WY.note: State law sets $5.15, but FLSA-covered employers must pay the $7.25 federal floor.

notes: Cities and counties may set local minimum wages above the state rate; the applicable wage for any employee is the highest of federal, state, and local.
Tipped minimum cash wages are not covered by this dataset; see DOL guidance for tip-credit rules by state.
